claims.text: Reviewers widely report that the product relieves pain, including nerve, joint, tendon, back, and muscle pain.
Many users find it effective for muscle soreness, strains, and workout-related aches.
Several reviewers note the cream is less messy and smells better than regular liquid DMSO, and some prefer the aloe/rose version because it doesn't burn.
A few reviewers mention skin irritation from the 99% liquid form and caution about washing hands and the application area.
Some users say it works best when combined with another topical product such as a menthol gel or aloe vera gel.

qa.q: Does it really help with pain relief?
qa.answer: Yes, multiple reviewers report pain relief: one says it got them back in the gym without pain [2], another says it helps their pain though not a huge amount [4], and others report success on knees, ankles, and sore muscles [5][6]. One reviewer notes it is best for burns and inflammation pain [1], and another is optimistic it is helping their SI joint pain after ten days [3].

qa.answer: The reviews describe the rose scent as pleasant rather than overpowering: one says the Rose Scented version "is not bad at all" [1] and another calls it a "nice scent" [4]. No review explicitly rates the scent as strong or mild, so the intensity is not directly addressed.
